land.text: Salerno, where Siconulf was proclaimed prince after Sicard's murder in 839; the rest of the principality was assigned only in the 851 division

predecessors.note: Salerno page: 'preceded by the Principality of Benevento'; infobox '840-851: Siconulf (first)'. Cliopatria's Duchy of Benevento row (577-1084) is the neighbour.

land.text: the whole principality, which after 1077 'was completely merged into the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria'

successors.note: Gisulf II lost 'his city and his principality to the Guiscard' in 1077; the city submitted on 13 December 1076 and the citadel fell in May 1077. The Principality of Salerno was reconstituted only as a fief in 1139 (Salerno page), outside this dossier.

capitals.name: Salerno
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Salerno'; Siconulf was proclaimed prince in Salerno.

correction.text: Salerno and its district, Siconulf's seat during the civil war of 839-851

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 840-850: Cliopatria's 840 shape (17,791 km2) is the lands assigned only by the 851 division. During the civil war 'Siconulf was proclaimed prince in Salerno while the assassin Radelchis took the throne in Benevento'; the page names no other town held by Siconulf. No infobox area.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 840 shape (Cosenza, Conza, Potenza, Paestum, Sarno) with Capua, as the Divisio of 851 assigned them; Taranto is named by the page but is not in the shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 851-860: in 851 Louis II divided the principality; 'Salerno consisted of Taranto, Cassano, Cosenza, Paestum, Conza, Potenza, Sarno...' and the Capua page adds that 'Capua is included as a part of Salerno' (Divisio of Louis II) until Pando declared it independent in 861. Cliopatria's 840 shape has no Capua cells and no Taranto cells.

Right as a shape for 861-879 (Capua independent from 861, no Capua cells): the pages date no change in 880. For 840-850 see the Salerno-only keyframe above and for 851-860 the one with Capua. The area has no infobox figure to compare.

Within a single cell of the 840 shape (17,574 against 17,791 km2); the pages give no event for 880. The shape holds until the Byzantine theme of Lucania is formed (c. 968), so it is valid for 880-967 only. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 880..967 from this entry's own 'valid for 880-967 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the Cliopatria 970 shape (Salerno, Cilento and the Irpinian edge), valid from c. 968 to 979

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria cuts the principality from 17,574 to 5,063 km2 (the Potenza, Conza and Cosenza interior, 10,622 km2) in 970. The Theme of Lucania page says the theme was 'established probably c. 968', 'roughly modern Basilicata'. The shape is right but starts about two years earlier, in 968. Cosenza is not on that page.

correction.text: the principality as in the 990 shape, under Pandulf II (978-981), Manso I of Amalfi (981-983) and John son of Lambert (983 on)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 980-989: Cliopatria has no shape for 980-989. The principality was under 'foreigners' 978-983: Pandulf II (son of Pandulf Ironhead) from 978, the Amalfitans (Manso I) from 981, and the Salernitans elected John, son of Lambert, in 983. The land is unchanged; drawn as the 990 shape.
Right for 990-1037 (5,232 km2; the pages date no frontier change). From May 1038 Guaimar IV also held Capua, so 1038-1045 is replaced by the next keyframes.

correction.text: Salerno with Capua (from May 1038), Amalfi (from April 1039) and Benevento (1040, one page only)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1038-1046: Guaimar IV was 'Prince of Capua (1038-1047)' after Conrad II gave him the principality in May 1038, 'Duke of Amalfi (1039-1052)' from April 1039, and (Benevento page) took control of Benevento in 1040; the Guaimar page does not mention Benevento. Gaeta (June 1040 to after October 1041), Traetto, Venafro, Aquino, Sora are not drawn. Cliopatria shows none of this: Capua gets its own shape in 1034-1039 and nothing for 1040-1055. [Reviewer eu-13-e, 2026-10-25: the Capua part is now Cliopatria's 1034 Capua shape minus Gaeta, so that Gaeta is not drawn for 1038-1046 as this note intends; the June 1040 gain and October 1041 loss carry it.]

correction.text: Salerno with Amalfi, after Capua is returned in 1047

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1047-1051: Henry III 'returned Capua to Pandulf' in 1047; Guaimar kept Amalfi to 1052. Benevento is dropped at 1047 on the Guaimar page's silence (confidence 1 in the ledger).

Valid for 1052-1055: Guaimar IV, Prince of Salerno 1027-1052, was assassinated in 1052 (2-4 June, the sources differ) and his son Gisulf II succeeded. Amalfi's duke title ended with him. Cliopatria starts this shape in 1046, one year before Capua is returned.
5,400 km2 and the same cells as 990; the pages date no change between 1052 and 1076. Gisulf II reigned 1052-1077 and 'Salerno declined'.
Same cells as 1056; no change recorded on the pages.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1072 shape, valid for 1072-1076 (the city fell December 1076, the citadel May 1077)

keyframe_review.note: Valid 1072-1076 only. 'On 13 December 1076, the city submitted' to Robert Guiscard and 'the citadel, which fell in May 1077'; Cliopatria draws the principality to 1084, seven years too long. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1072..1076 from this entry's own 'Valid 1072-1076 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: Salerno, where Siconulf was proclaimed prince

ledger.note: 840: Siconulf is proclaimed prince at Salerno. 'Sicard's brother, Siconulf, was proclaimed prince in Salerno while the assassin Radelchis took the throne in Benevento' after Sicard's murder in 839; the Salerno infobox lists '840-851: Siconulf (first)'.

region.text: the frontier between Salerno and Benevento in the civil war

ledger.note: 840-851: the civil war. 'When Sicard was assassinated in 839, a civil war broke out'; 'After 10 years of civil war, Emperor Louis II ended the conflict'. The page names no town taken.

region.text: the frontier between Salerno and Benevento

ledger.note: 851: Louis II divides the principality. 'In 851, Louis, King of Italy, divided the principality into two sections.' The Capua page puts the decree in 849 and the Divisio in 851; the Benevento page says only 'after 10 years of civil war'.

region.text: 'Salerno consisted of Taranto, Cassano, Cosenza, Paestum, Conza, Potenza, Sarno...'; Capua is included

ledger.note: 851: the division gives Salerno the southern lands. The page lists the places; the region is the Cliopatria 840 shape (which has no Taranto cells) and Capua. The Benevento page: 'As a part of the partition, Capua was made part of the Principality of Salerno.'
861: Capua breaks away. 'In 861, Pando the Rapacious declared Capua independent of Salerno.' The Salerno page says only that Capua 'made itself independent' in Guaifer's reign.

region.text: the Basilicata interior (the Theme of Lucania, 'roughly modern Basilicata') and the Cosenza edge

ledger.note: c. 968: the Byzantines form the Theme of Lucania. 'established probably c. 968, under emperor Nikephoros II Phokas'; it 'corresponds roughly to modern Basilicata'. The page does not say the land came from Salerno or mention Cosenza; the region is Cliopatria's 970 loss. [Reviewer eu-13-e, 2026-10-25: confidence lowered to 1: the Theme of Lucania page says the theme 'was formed to encompass Lombard-populated areas of the theme of Longobardia' (Byzantine land) and does not name Salerno, so the loss rests on Cliopatria's 970 cut alone.]

978: Pandulf II of the Capuan house succeeds. 'Gisulf I died, and Salerno passed to Pandulf Ironhead's son, Pandulf II'; infobox: 'The principality is under the rule of foreigners: 978-983.' Same state, same colour (rule 2).
981: Amalfi takes Salerno. 'The Amalfitans took advantage of the Ironhead's death in 981 to seize it from Pandulf II.' Manso I of Amalfi became prince. Same state.
983: the Salernitans choose their own prince. 'Salernitans elected John, son of Lambert, after expelling the Amalfitans.' Independence restored; same state.

region.text: Capua, given to Guaimar IV by Conrad II, without Gaeta (held by Pandulf's party until Guaimar took it in June 1040)

ledger.note: May 1038: Guaimar IV becomes Prince of Capua. 'Capua was promptly besieged' by Conrad II, who 'having taken the principality' gave it to Guaimar (May 1038); lead: 'Prince of Capua (1038-1047)'. [Reviewer eu-13-e, 2026-10-25: region excludes Gaeta: the Guaimar IV page says 'In June 1040, he took Gaeta, which had been conquered by Pandulf in 1032', so Gaeta was not part of the May 1038 grant; it enters with the 1040 gain and leaves with the 1041 loss.]

April 1039: Guaimar IV becomes Duke of Amalfi. 'In April 1039' he forced the abdication of John II and 'installed himself as duke'; lead: 'Duke of Amalfi (1039-1052)'. The Amalfi dossier (Cliopatria's row ends 1033) must carry the matching loss.

1040: 'The Prince of Salerno Guaimar IV took control of Benevento in 1040' (Benevento page). The Guaimar IV page does not mention it, so the extent and the end of the hold are unsupported: see the 1047 loss.

region.text: Gaeta, taken by Guaimar IV (a place the gazetteer lacks)

ledger.note: June 1040: Guaimar takes Gaeta. 'In June 1040, he took Gaeta, which had been conquered by Pandulf in 1032'; lead: 'Duke of Gaeta (1040-1041)'. No Gaeta shape or dossier exists; the keyframes do not draw it.
After October 1041: Gaeta slips away. 'After October 1041, Guaimar ceases to appear in the acts of Gaeta.' By December 1042 Gaeta was held by Rainulf from Guaimar.

region.text: the Norman lordships of Aversa and Melfi, which acclaimed Guaimar IV 'Duke of Apulia and Calabria'

ledger.note: 1043: the Normans acclaim Guaimar. They 'acclaimed him Duke of Apulia and Calabria (1043)'; 'Guaimar ... granted them Melfi'. The vassal tint is the researcher's reading of the feudal grant; Cliopatria's Norman shape for 1043 is Aversa only.

region.text: Capua, returned to Pandulf by Henry III

ledger.note: 1047: Henry III undoes Guaimar's work. 'He returned Capua to Pandulf and took Aversa and Melfi directly under his suzerainty.'
1047: Henry III 'deprived Guaimar of his title over Apulia and Calabria' and took Aversa and Melfi under his own suzerainty; in 1048 Guaimar 'recaptured the allegiance of Aversa'.
1047 on the bridge: the Guaimar page says only that in 1047 'The emperor also besieged Benevento'; the Benevento page gives no end to the 1040 hold. Placed at 1047 with the rest of Guaimar's work.

1052: Guaimar IV is assassinated in the harbour of Salerno (2, 3 or 4 June, the sources differ) and his dukedom of Amalfi, held 1039-1052, ends with him; Gisulf II succeeds as prince, 'whom the Normans put under their protection'.

region.text: the city of Salerno, submitted to Robert Guiscard

ledger.note: 13 December 1076: Salerno submits. 'On 13 December 1076, the city submitted'; the siege began earlier (the page does not date its start).

region.text: the citadel and the whole principality

ledger.note: May 1077: the citadel falls. 'the citadel, which fell in May 1077'; the Salerno page: Gisulf II 'lost his city and his principality to the Guiscard' and the domain was 'completely merged into the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria'.
1077: the Lombard principality ends. Infobox: 'The city and principality are conquered by the Normans: 1077.' Cliopatria's last shape runs to 1084.

wars.name: Civil war of the Beneventan succession (Radelchis I against Siconulf)
wars.outcome: Louis II divided the principality in 851 into Benevento and Salerno; Salerno received Taranto, Cassano, Cosenza, Paestum, Conza, Potenza and Sarno, and Capua.
wars.note: The Capua page dates Louis II's decree to 849 and the Divisio to 851; the Benevento page counts ten years of war from 839. The Salerno infobox gives Siconulf as prince 840-851.

wars.name: Conrad II's expedition to Capua
wars.outcome: Conrad II, invited south by Guaimar IV, besieged Capua and gave the principality to Guaimar in May 1038; Henry III reversed this in 1047.
wars.note: The page does not use the words 'deposition' or 'investiture'; 'Capua was promptly besieged' after hostages escaped.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Salerno

zones.text: the principality, city 13 December 1076, citadel May 1077

wars.outcome: Robert Guiscard took the city (December 1076) and the citadel (May 1077); the principality was merged into the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria.
wars.note: The Amalfitans had summoned the Guiscard against their own duke in 1073 (same page). The start of the siege is not dated on the pages opened.

certainty.note: The 851 division of Louis II named the gastaldates assigned to each prince but fixed no surveyed line; the Basilicata frontier with the Byzantine theme and the Capuan frontier were never delimited on the pages opened.

notes: Page budget (5) exceeded by two: the Duchy of Benevento page was a miss (it ends in 774) and the Capua and Guaimar IV pages were opened for the Capua dossier and reused here; no event rests on a search snippet. No page gives an infobox area, so the area comparison could not be made. Cliopatria rows: the 840 shape (17,791 km2) is drawn from 840, but Siconulf held only Salerno until the 851 division and Capua was part of Salerno 851-860 (no Capua cells in the shape; no Taranto cells either although the page lists Taranto); the 970 cut matches the Theme of Lucania c. 968; Cliopatria has no shape for 980-989 and none for Guaimar IV's union with Capua, Amalfi and Benevento (1038-1047); the last shape runs to 1084 though Salerno fell in 1077. The Aghlabid neighbour 850-874 and the Byzantine border before 968 are not on any page opened. Guaimar IV's northern holdings (Traetto May 1039, Venafro October 1040, Aquino, Sora, Pontecorvo, Comino) and Gaeta are not drawn: they have no dossier or gazetteer name (Gaeta, Melfi, Aversa, Squillace, Teano, Sora are missing from places.jsonl). The Benevento page says Guaimar took Benevento in 1040 while the Guaimar page is silent: confidence 2/1. Rulers are omitted: no page lists the princes with reign years. 'Duchy of Gaeta' needs a dossier (counterpart string used).
